description.narrative: The project is implemented in Turkey. The main outcome areas it contributes to are peace and dialogue. The main right holders are civil society actors and the academia. Through trainings, organising and mobilising, advocacy and capacity building the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between Hrant Dink Foundation in Turkey, The Worker's Educational Association (ABF) in Södertälje and the Palme Center.The local partner organisation Hrant Dink Foundation works primarily with anti discrimination, peace building and developing capacities of the civil society organisations in Turkey. The ABF-Södertälje, one of the Palme Center's member organisations, is highly engaged in the development in Turkey, with a memberbase intrested in contribution to the democratic development. They support this partnership with their specific focus on and expertise in adcovacy and networking and will function as a channel to relevant organisations in Sweden and Europe. The Palme Center will support the project with administrative and technical support.Other Donors to the OrganisationThere are no other donors in the project. The organisation as such has other donors, such as EU-funding.Project ObjectiveThe project objective is to contribute to the normalisation of relations between Turkey and Armenia. The project aims to 1) build confidence between key actors in the both countries, 2) establish thematic working groups, in order to ensure the engagement of civil society actors, academic institutions and subject-experts from Armenia and Turkey in the process of normalisation of relations between the two neighbouring countries, 3) develop new spin-off projects and commission further research and field studies in order to put into action priority confidence building measures, aiming at the normalisation of relations between the two neighbours, 4) draft new confidence building measures and recommendations 5) engage with policy-makers in Armenia, Turkey and Europe to communicate its recommendations and to further map out the needs in various fields towards normalisation of Armenia-Turkey relations, 6) carry out its initiatives to the next level, by introducing its work and proposed confidence building measures to the stakeholders in Europe and the USA.Actor groupsThe main actor group in the project are civil society actors that work on peace and peace building, the academia and governmental bodies in Turkey and Armenia.The organisations main actors within the group of, 1) right holders are: human rights actors within the civil society organisations.2) actors working in cooperation: the civil society organisations and the academia in Turkey, international organisations working on peace building such as EU, UN and CoE) who have the potential to mobilize their instruments in a constructive way to open new channels of communication between Turkey and Armenia, and encouraging them to establish relations with each other.3) decision makers: the government agencies and the political leadership in the political parties.
